correctness.rationale: For each sparse window, partition sampled indices by residue modulo m. Active start phases sample only binary Sturmian coordinates, with disjoint supports across different phases; their t sampled coordinates have at most 2t patterns from the 2t interval endpoints and can attain 2t by choosing distinct irrational-rotation indices with entrances grouped before exits. Inactive phases each yield one q-letter signature; their exact number is D_c(S). Disjoint alphabets exclude overlaps, giving p*_y(k)=2k+max_{|S|<=k}D_c(S) for every k, including k=1 and k>=m. For |S|=t there are m-t inactive phases and q^t possible words: D<=min(m-t,q^t). Setting s=min{1<=s<=m:q^s>=m-s}, the minima on t<s and t>=s yield min(q^k,m-s). An order-min(k,s) q-ary de Bruijn cycle, repeated across the m-1 decorative positions, realizes all available consecutive t-words. This is an infinite proof; my independently coded exhaustive signature enumerator confirmed all 41 q,m,k triples with q=2,m=2..7 and q=3,m=2..5, not an argument for all cases.
residual_risks: Finite independent tests do not certify any unrestricted theorem; analytical argument and published structural lemmas carry generality.
